land.text: the Rouran steppe: 74% of the Göktürk 555 shape (14,281 of 19,248 cells) lies inside the Rouran 554 shape

predecessors.note: Bumin defeated Anagui in 552 (First Turkic Khaganate page: infobox "Predecessor: Rouran Khaganate; Hephthalite Empire"); the Rouran page has the Turks occupy the Rouran in 555, the year Cliopatria hands the land over.

land.text: the Hephthalite land (Transoxiana, Sogdia, Bactria north of the Oxus, Khwarezm, Fergana) that Cliopatria hands from the White Huns 555 shape to the Göktürk 561 shape

predecessors.note: Taken about 557-560 with the Sasanians (Hephthalites page: "Around 560 CE their empire was destroyed by an alliance of the First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanian Empire"), not at the birth in 552; Cliopatria draws it from 561.

land.text: the eastern half "still ruled from Ötüken", the Mongolian Plateau

successors.note: First Turkic Khaganate page: "When the fourth ruler of the khaganate, Taspar Qaghan, died in 581, the realm split in two over his succession"; the formal division is 603. Cliopatria dates the two successors from 587.

land.text: the western half ruled by Tardu, capital Suyab in the Chu valley, from the Tarim basin to the Caspian

successors.note: Tardu "made a bid for total independence"; the Western Turkic Khaganate page calls it an administrative region of the First Turkic Khaganate (581-603) and an independent empire (603-657).

capitals.name: Ötüken (Orkhon valley, Mongolia)
capitals.note: Infobox "Capital: Ötüken (eastern); Suyab (western)". The Ötüken site is the Orkhon valley near modern Kharkhorin (the Second Turkic Khaganate page: "centered on Ötüken in the upper reaches of the Orkhon River"); the point is approximate. The page gives no years for Suyab (42.8 N, 75.2 E, Chu valley), the western seat.

rulers.name: Bumin (Illig Khagan)
rulers.note: First Turkic Khaganate page: Bumin "declared himself Illig Khagan of the new Khaganate at Ötüken, but died only months later".

rulers.name: Ishbara Qaghan
rulers.note: The Eastern Turkic Khaganate page gives 581-587; the row ends in 586 in Cliopatria. The western co-rulers Istämi (552-575) and Tardu (575-603) are not strip entries; the First Turkic page lists both twice.

correction.text: Ötüken, the seat of the new khaganate, 552-554

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Göktürk row begins in 555 but the page dates the khaganate to 552. Bumin 'declared himself Illig Khagan of the new Khaganate at Ötüken' after defeating Anagui in 552, and the Rouran still held ground until 555 (Rouran page: the Turks invaded and occupied the Rouran in 555), so only the Orkhon core is drawn; the contested plateau comes from the ledger (contest 552-555).

4.98 M km2 for 555-560 against the infobox 6.0 M km2 for 557 (ratio 0.83, within the factor of two). 74% of the shape (14,281 of 19,248 cells) is the Rouran 554 shape, handed over in 555 (ledger); the Hephthalite land is not yet in it. The page is silent on 555 itself ('effectively ended the Rouran' in 552).

6.42 M km2 for 561-576 against 6.0 M km2 at 557 (ratio 1.07). The 5,005 added cells are the Hephthalite land (3,202 cells of the White Huns 555 shape) plus the Kazakh and Pontic steppe to the Don; the Hephthalites page dates the fall 'around 560'. The Western Turkic Khaganate page puts the takeover of the steppe between the Caspian and the Black Sea at c. 567-576, so 561-566 may be early there (unverified). The Crimean campaign ('In 576 the Göktürks crossed the Kerch Strait into the Crimea', Chersonesus besieged 'five years later', roaming until 590) lies west of the shape (edge 37.8 E) and is not drawn.

6.42 M km2, the 561 shape again. The page records no border change for 577-586; the civil war after Taspar's death in 581 ('the realm split in two') is why Cliopatria ends the row in 586 and draws the Eastern and Western Göktürks from 587.

region.text: Ötüken, the upper Orkhon valley, where Bumin proclaimed the khaganate

ledger.note: 552: Bumin defeats Anagui and proclaims the Turkic khaganate at Ötüken. 'In 552, Bumin defeated Anagui and his forces north of Huaihuang'; he 'declared himself Illig Khagan of the new Khaganate at Ötüken, but died only months later'; infobox 'Established: 552'. The text dates the origins to 546 and the infobox gives Bumin's revolt as 542; the page does not reconcile them. Ötüken is read as the Orkhon valley.

region.text: the steppe of the Rouran, contested from 552 to 555

ledger.note: 552: the Turks and the Rouran fight for the steppe. The page has the 552 victory north of Huaihuang but no later campaign; the Rouran page has Issik 'continued attacks' to 553 and the Turks occupying the Rouran in 555.

region.text: the Yenisei Kyrgyz homeland: Tuva and the Minusinsk Hollow (Yenisei Kyrgyz page)

ledger.note: 553: the Yenisei Kyrgyz under Turkic control. The Eastern Turkic Khaganate page says only that Muqan (553-572) 'controlled the Yenisei Kyrgyz'; no date for the subjection, so the first year of the reign stands (confidence 1). The Yenisei Kyrgyz page is silent on it. The Kyrgyz stay Turkic vassals under the successors (ledger 586).

region.text: the steppe of the Rouran, contested from 552 to 555

ledger.note: 555: the Rouran steppe is the Turks'. In 555 the Turks invaded and occupied the Rouran (Rouran page); Muqan Qaghan had Dengshuzi and his men handed over by Western Wei and the Rouran were annihilated.

region.text: the part of the Rouran steppe that Cliopatria's Göktürk 555 shape holds: Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, without the Hebei, Liaoning, Jilin and Shanxi edge of the Rouran 554 shape (1,972 cells)

ledger.note: 555: the Turks take the Rouran steppe. Rouran page: the khaganate 'ended when they were defeated by a Göktürk rebellion'; 'In 555 ... Turks invaded and occupied the Rouran'; Eastern Turkic Khaganate page: Muqan 'finished off the remaining Rouran (who resisted until 555)' and 'pushed the Kitans east', so the Manchurian and north-China edge of the Cliopatria Rouran shape is not drawn as Turkic. Narrowed on 1 Nov 2026 (fx-24, snap F033) from the whole Rouran 554 shape to its overlap with Cliopatria's Göktürk 555 shape (14,281 cells).

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's Göktürk 555 shape: the Kazakh steppe (Qaraghandy, Aqtöbe, East Kazakhstan, Almaty, Zhambyl) and a strip of Inner Mongolia beyond the Rouran 554 shape (4,967 cells)

ledger.note: 555: the Turks hold the Rouran country beyond the Cliopatria Rouran 554 outline. Rouran page: the Rouran territory 'covered all of modern-day Mongolia and Inner Mongolia' and included 'parts of Manchuria in Northeast China, Eastern Siberia, Xinjiang, and Kazakhstan'; the page gives no border, so the extent of these 4,967 cells is Cliopatria's Göktürk 555 shape, set in the ledger on 1 Nov 2026 (fx-24, snap F033) so that the 555 keyframe is no longer a jump from the ledger. Confidence 1: the page names Kazakhstan only in general.

region.text: the Hephthalite country north of the Hindu Kush: Transoxiana and Bactria

ledger.note: 557: Turks and Sasanians move on the Hephthalites. Hephthalites page: a combined defeat 'is dated (557 CE)'; First Turkic page: 'In 557, Istämi forged an alliance with Khosrow I of the Sassanid Empire ... to defeat and destroy the Hephthalites'. The year of the first campaign that took ground is not given.

region.text: the Hephthalite land (Transoxiana, Sogdia, Bactria north of the Oxus, Khwarezm, Fergana) that Cliopatria hands from the White Huns 555 shape to the Göktürk 561 shape

ledger.note: 560: the Hephthalite land passes to the Turks. 'Around 560 CE their empire was destroyed by an alliance of the First Turkic Khaganate and the Sasanian Empire'; after 560 the Hephthalite principalities were under Western Turk suzerainty north of the Oxus and Sasanian suzerainty south of it. Cliopatria draws the land in the Göktürk shape from 561.
560: the fighting for the Hephthalite land ends with the empire destroyed 'around 560 CE'; the Alchon Huns page gives 557-565 for the same alliance, so the end year is approximate.

region.text: the rest of the 561 additions: the Kazakh and Pontic steppe west of the Aral Sea to the Don (west edge 37.8 E)

ledger.note: 561: the Turks hold the steppe to the Don. Western Turkic Khaganate page: 'the Turks took the area between the Caspian and Black Seas' (c. 567-576) with Panticapaeum the westernmost point; Cliopatria draws this steppe from 561, six years before the page's earliest date, so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Yenisei Kyrgyz homeland: Tuva and the Minusinsk Hollow (Yenisei Kyrgyz page)

ledger.note: 586: the relation is closed with the state. The pages opened give no end to the subjection and are silent on the Kyrgyz between Muqan's reign and the Second Turkic Khaganate's victory of 709-710 (Second Turkic Khaganate page), so the vassal line is closed here at Cliopatria's end year (confidence 1).

region.text: the Mongolian Plateau and the southern steppe

ledger.note: 586: the eastern half becomes its own khaganate. 'When the fourth ruler of the khaganate, Taspar Qaghan, died in 581, the realm split in two over his succession'; the eastern part 'still ruled from Ötüken, remained in the orbit of the Sui and retained the name Göktürk'. Cliopatria dates the new state from 587; the infobox gives the Eastern khaganate as founded 581.

region.text: Central Asia from the Altai to the Black Sea steppe

ledger.note: 586: the western half becomes its own khaganate. Tardu 'made a bid for total independence' and 'led an army east to claim the seat of imperial power, Ötüken'; the western capital was Suyab in the Chu valley. The page gives the final division as 603 ('Division of Western and Eastern Turkic Khaganates: 603'); Cliopatria dates the western state from 587.

586: the First Turkic Khaganate ends in Cliopatria's reckoning; the page has it split in 581 and formally divided in 603 ('The Khaganate collapsed in 603'). Its land goes to the Eastern and Western Göktürks.

wars.name: Göktürk revolt against the Rouran

zones.text: the steppe of the Rouran, contested from 552 to 555

wars.outcome: Bumin defeated Anagui in 552 (Anagui killed himself); the Turks occupied the Rouran in 555 and Muqan had the Rouran remnant destroyed.
wars.note: Rouran page: Bumin, allied with Western Wei, attacked the Rouran in 552 after a dispute over a princess; the Gaoche page dates a Tiele revolt that Bumin crushed to 546, the Rouran page to 551. The First Turkic page dates the origins to 546 and the infobox revolt to 542.

wars.name: Göktürk-Sasanian war against the Hephthalites

zones.text: the Hephthalite country on both sides of the Oxus

wars.outcome: The Hephthalite empire was destroyed 'around 560'; the Turks took the land north of the Oxus and the Sasanians suzerainty south of it.
wars.note: Alchon Huns page gives the alliance's defeat of the Alchon as 557-565.

wars.name: Göktürk civil war
wars.outcome: The realm divided into an eastern part (Ötüken, Sui orbit) and a western part (Tardu, Suyab); the formal division is 603, with a brief reunification under Tardu 599-603 (Eastern Turkic page).
wars.note: No border moved inside the Cliopatria years 555-586; the successors are drawn from 587.

wars.name: Göktürk campaign in the Crimea
wars.outcome: The Turks crossed the Kerch Strait in 576, besieged Chersonesus five years later and roamed the Crimean steppe until 590; no land is drawn, the shape stops at 37.8 E.
wars.note: Western Turkic Khaganate page: Panticapaeum was the westernmost point of the Turkic realm.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; no treaty line is dated by the pages. The western edge (Don, Crimea) and the Oxus frontier with the Sasanians are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria row Göktürk Khaganate 555..586 (3 shapes). The page dates the khaganate to 552 (infobox 'Established: 552'; the origins in 546 in the text, Bumin's revolt in 542 in the infobox), so a core keyframe 552-554 is added and the Rouran steppe is a contested zone until 555. The row ends in 586 while the pages put the split in 581 (civil war) and the division in 603; the dossier keeps Cliopatria's 586/587 handover and records the page dates in the notes of the split and dissolve events (confidence 1). The Eastern and Western Göktürks are two states, not one (Western Turkic Khaganate page: 'Within 35 years the Western Turkic Khaganate and the Eastern Turkic Khaganate were independent polities'); they share Wikidata Q205466 (Göktürks) only. Not drawn: the Crimean campaign (576-590), west of the shape; Turkic suzerainty over the Avars ('the slaves of the Turks', 558) and tribute from Northern Zhou/Northern Qi (page silent). Pages opened beyond the 1-2 page budget (Rouran, Hephthalites, Eastern Turkic, Western Turkic) were opened for the neighbouring dossiers of the same batch and are cited only for the events listed. Counterpart needing a dossier: none new; the Rouran, White Huns and Eastern/Western Göktürks are in this and the next batch. The Kyrgyz vassalage (553-586) is recorded here, with the suzerain; the vassal's own dossier cannot carry it, and the pages are silent on the Kyrgyz after 586 until 709-710.
